items.summary: Persistent Context Across Sessions for Every Agent – Captures everything your agent does during sessions, compresses it with AI, and injects relevant context back into future sessions. Works with Claude Code, OpenClaw, Codex, Gemini, Hermes, Copilot, OpenCode + More

This enables Claude to maintain continuity of knowledge about projects even after sessions end or reconnect. --- ## Quick Start Install claude-mem for Grok Bot: ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide grok-bot ``` Grok Bot has no host hooks, so we watch the chat log files. items.summary: Use Garry Tan's exact Claude Code setup: 23 opinionated tools that serve as CEO, Designer, Eng Manager, Release Manager, Doc Engineer, and QA
items.excerpt: # gstack > "I don't think I've typed like a line of code probably since December, basically, which is an extremely large change." — [Andrej Karpathy](https://fortune.com/2026/03/21/andrej-karpathy-openai-cofounder-ai-agents-coding-state-of-psychosis-openclaw/), No Priors podcast, March 2026 When I heard Karpathy say this, I wanted to find out how. How does one person ship like a team of twenty? Peter Steinberger built [OpenClaw](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw) — 247K GitHub stars — essentially solo with AI agents. The revolution is here. A single builder with the right tooling can move faster than a traditional team. I'm [Garry Tan](https://x.com/garrytan), President & CEO of [Y Combinator](https://www.ycombinator.com/). I've worked with thousands of startups — Coinbase, Instacart, Rippling — when they were one or two people in a garage. Before YC, I was one of the first eng/PM/designers at Palantir, cofounded Posterous (sold to Twitter), and built Bookface, YC's internal social network. **gstack is my answer.** I've been building products for twenty years, and right now I'm shipping more products than I ever have. In the last 60 days: 3 production services, 40+ shipped features, part-time, while running YC full-time. On logical code change — not raw LOC, which AI inflates — my 2026 run rate is **~810× my 2013 pace** (11,417 vs 14 logical lines/day). Year-to-date (through April 18), 2026 has already produced **240× the entire 2013 year**. Measured across 40 public +…

items.title: The Biggest AI Coding Agent Upgrade Is Already on Your Machine?!
items.summary: Every conversation you have with your coding agent is saved as a file on your machine - every prompt, every tool call, every failure. It's a goldmine of data that almost nobody takes advantage of, and it's the best way I've found to make my coding agent better over time. So in this video I show you two ways to use it! The simple way is one prompt that has your coding agent go through your past conversations and suggest the top improvements for your rules, hooks, and skills. The full way puts everything into structured tables in a database (I use Databricks), so you can easily query it with your coding agent and MCP. It's super token efficient too! I also show you the real changes I made to my own AI layer from it (I'm actually keeping every one of them). ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ - Check out Databricks Free Edition - free to use, no credit card, and everything in this video runs on it: https://databricks.plug.dev/xLkLORm Thanks to Databricks for working with me on this video! Btw - the "not used to train" commitment I show ~10 minutes in is from Databricks' paid terms. Free Edition has its own terms that let Databricks use what you upload to improve their services and AI models, so scrub anything sensitive first (or have your coding agent do it like I talk about!). ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ - Join Dynamous for the new Agentic Coding Course 2.0 - the core of the course is now COMPLETE: https://dynamous.ai - The opportunity-scan skill, the simple one-prompt version…

items.title: You Built Your AI Second Brain. Now What? (Here's How to Evolve It)
items.summary: An AI second brain works for one person. Once a whole team needs one, that stops being true. And you can't simply just build a "bigger" second brain. The team needs a different layer underneath, and this video is about that layer - the team brain. I show you how the team brain works: how information from chat platforms, repos, and docs goes in a single table, how search over that table works, how every row gets labeled, and how the database enforces those labels on every read for security and permissions. Then your coding agent queries it over MCP with its own token, and your own second brain keeps its memory system and personality on top! I use Oracle AI Database to show it, but the structure works with the tools you already have. The full code is linked below and you can run on the free Oracle AI DB container. ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ Check out the Oracle AI Developer Hub on GitHub - a ton of great resources for building with the Oracle AI Database and more: https://fandf.co/4A9r6Km Thanks to Oracle for partnering with me on this one! ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ - Join Dynamous for the new Agentic Coding Course 2.0 - the core of the course is now COMPLETE: https://dynamous.ai - The Team Brain code, my PR into the hub: https://github.com/coleam00/oracle-ai-developer-hub/tree/team-brain/apps/team-brain - LangChain + Oracle AI Database docs: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/integrations/vectorstores/oracle The langchain-oracle package…

items.title: Dashboards Are Dead — Sarah Simionescu, Composio
items.summary: Sarah used Datadog every day for six months without ever opening the dashboard. Sarah Simionescu, member of technical staff at Composio and on the team behind the Composio dashboard, makes the case that the dashboard is dead. She traces how we got here: five tools and five query languages, then the AI 'sparkle button', then MCP. She explains why MCP alone is still a mess (agents don't learn, too many tools drown the model, every app is isolated) and shows how an interface designed for agents fixes it. Live demos go from a Slack bug report to a fix PR, and run a cross-app analysis across PostHog and Metabase without loading full results into context. In this talk: • Why every dashboard and query language was a translation layer • Three reasons wiring up a dozen MCP servers falls apart • How tool search plus execution plans help agents work across apps • Building products for a new kind of user: agents SPEAKER Sarah Simionescu, Member of Technical Staff, Composio LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/sarah-simionescu/ GitHub: https://github.com/sarahsimionescu Website: https://www.sarahsimionescu.com/ LINKS Composio: https://composio.dev/ Composio MCP: https://composio.dev/mcp-gateway CHAPTERS 0:00 Intro 0:12 A confession about dashboards 1:02 The dashboard is dead 1:17 A postmortem 1:27 2022: five tools, five query languages 2:17 You wanted the answer, not the dashboard 2:37 2023: the sparkle button 3:02 2024: MCP arrives 3:31 Why MCP alone is a mess 3:51 Agents don't learn…

She traces how we got here: five tools and five query languages, then the AI 'sparkle button', then MCP. She explains why MCP alone is still a mess (agents don't learn, too many tools drown the model, every app is isolated) and shows how an interface designed for agents fixes it. Live demos go from a Slack bug report to a fix PR, and run a cross-app analysis across PostHog and Metabase without loading full results into context. In this talk: • Why every dashboard and query language was a translation layer • Three reasons wiring up a dozen MCP servers falls apart • How tool search plus execution plans help agents work across apps • Building products for a new kind of user: agents SPEAKER Sarah Simionescu, Member of Technical Staff, Composio LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/sarah-simionescu/ GitHub: https://github.com/sarahsimionescu Website: https://www.sarahsimionescu.com/ LINKS Composio: https://composio.dev/ Composio MCP: https://composio.dev/mcp-gateway CHAPTERS 0:00 Intro 0:12 A confession about dashboards 1:02 The dashboard is dead 1:17 A postmortem 1:27 2022: five tools, five query languages 2:17 You wanted the answer, not the dashboard 2:37 2023: the sparkle button 3:02 2024: MCP arrives 3:31 Why MCP alone is a mess 3:51 Agents don't learn…

We set up Karpathy's loop on our own apps, found the one issue it can't see, and fixed it with a loop that improves itself. It's the step past prompt engineering for agentic AI and AI automation. Community with All Resources: https://ailabspro.io/?v=qLfSDQ5NGh0 The Roundup, our daily newsletter covering the AI stories that matter. Join now: https://www.theroundup.so/ WTF is loop engineering? It's building agentic loops: an AI agent makes a change, a separate check scores it, and the agent keeps the change only if the score improves. Loop AI engineering took off with Andrej Karpathy's AutoResearch. His agent was allowed to change only one training file and could never touch the file that scored it. A plain-English file called program.md told it how to run each round. Over two days it ran 700 experiments and found 20 changes that made the model train faster. Shopify's CEO ran the same kind of loop on one of his own models overnight: 37 experiments, and the model performed 19% better by morning. This is a full long video on loop engineering. Before the setup, we cover when a loop is worth building at all. The task should be one you repeat often. You need a usage limit that can handle the token cost. The work has to be checkable without a human…
